purpose: Clarifies the boundary between requirements (What) and design (How) documents and supports deciding where content belongs, with severity catalog, gray-zone tolerances, and traceability norms.
summary: Basic principles contrasting requirements (What) and design (How) documents
Relationship with ADRs: design states current design, ADR holds rationale
Decision criteria: already decided with no choice goes to requirements, then user manual test
Category guides for quantitative goals and feature rationale and value
Severity catalog for What/How boundary violations and diagram or type gray zones
Gray-zone tolerances for data model types, diagrams, and quantitative goals
Lightweight traceability norms for design reviews
Approval record rule: design adding features absent from requirements needs a linked ADR
Additive development treats the diff-side requirements as the current spec
tasks: Deciding whether content belongs in requirements or design
Reviewing requirements or design for boundary violations
Writing quantitative targets such as performance goals
Checking design traceability to requirement IDs
title: 要件定義書と設計書の境界ガイド
